characters: Clement Duodu: a 15-year-old boy in a white shirt covered in felt-pen signatures, with a clear pencil case.
Harriet Sarfo: a 15-year-old girl, his classmate, with an examination slip and a neat file.
Mr Anan: the form master, in a short-sleeved shirt, wiping his glasses.
The classroom: an empty JHS 3 room on the last afternoon, with a faded chart and a chalkboard that says “Good luck, Form 3”.

narrationPlan.voice: Excited, nervous, then fond student voices; a kind, proud voice for Mr Anan
narrationPlan.pace: Warm and a little emotional, steady at the exam morning (about 120 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: Gentle, nostalgic guitar with a distant school bell; an uplifting, hopeful tune at the end (placeholder)
culturalNotes: The students and teacher are invented. The story shows a general BECE-week mood; check the current exam rules (items allowed, timings and index-number procedures) with the school and examining body.
Signing school shirts at the end of exams is a common tradition; schools differ in how they allow it. The story encourages kind messages only.
The letter on page 7 is exam-safe: “Dear Mr Anan”, “Yours sincerely”, full words and a specific reason for thanks.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?
Check the exam-day checklist (two pens, pencil, ruler, mathematical set, index number) against the current WAEC BECE instructions for candidates.
Check that the story does not encourage defacing school property and that school policy on shirt signing is respected.
Check the farewell letter against the BECE marking scheme; the letter is a semi-formal thank-you.

teacherGuide.overview: A story about the last week before the BECE: nerves, exam-day habits, thanks and goodbyes. It models a warm, exam-safe farewell letter to a teacher.
learningGoals: Describe ways to manage exam nerves.
Write a thank-you letter to a teacher with a specific reason.
beforeReading: Ask: what is one thing you would like to thank a teacher for?
whileReading: At page 2, ask learners to add items to the checklist from the current exam instructions.
afterReading: Write a farewell letter to a teacher or friend.
Make a poster with five calm exam-day habits.
discussion: Why do we feel nervous before exams? What helps?
How can we say goodbye kindly?
reflection: What would you like to be remembered for in this school?

support: Provide a checklist template and a thank-you letter frame.
stretch: Write a short farewell speech for your class.

localiseThis: Use your examining body’s real instructions and your school’s real traditions for the last day.
